Let's denote the vectors of $U$ as ${u}_{1},\,{u}_{2}.$ To extend the given set to an orthonormal basis of ${R}^{3}$, we need to find a third vector $x$ such that $‖x‖=1,$ and

$$
{\begin{aligned}{u}_{1}\cdot x=0 \\ {u}_{2}\cdot x=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}{x}_{1}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}{x}_{3}=0 \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}{x}_{1}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}{x}_{2}+\frac{2}{\sqrt{6}}{x}_{3}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system above and reduce it to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & 0 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & 0 \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{6}} & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=\sqrt{5}\cdot {R}_{1} \\ {R}_{2}:=\sqrt{6}\cdot {R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & \frac{5}{2} & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns ($1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=-\frac{5}{2}{x}_{3},$ and from the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{2}{x}_{3}.$

So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2}{x}_{3} \\ -\frac{5}{2}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{3}=2,$ we obtain the vector 
$x=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -5 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ 

Now, we need to normalize $x.$ Notice that $‖x‖=\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(-5)^{2}+{2}^{2}}=\sqrt{30}.$ So, we normalize $x$ as follows:

$$
\frac{x}{‖x‖}=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{30}} \\ -\frac{5}{\sqrt{30}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{30}}\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, an orthonormal basis of ${R}^{3}$ is

$$
{[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ 0 \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{6}}\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{30}} \\ -\frac{5}{\sqrt{30}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{30}}\end{aligned}]}.
$$

Finally, $|{x}_{1}|+|{x}_{2}|+|{x}_{3}|=|-\frac{1}{\sqrt{30}}|+|-\frac{5}{\sqrt{30}}|+|\frac{2}{\sqrt{30}}|=\frac{8}{\sqrt{30}}.$
